findings.problem: ShardWorkflow status is a raw String combined with separate lifecycle booleans (is_validated, is_sent), allowing illegal state combinations such as is_sent=true with is_validated=false, or status="sent" with is_sent=false.
findings.failure_mode: Business logic can observe a shard marked as sent without ever being validated, or with a status string that contradicts the booleans. Any consumer of mark_sent cannot prove the shard was validated before being sent.
findings.fix: Replace (status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool) with a single ShardState enum that encodes transitions: Pending -> Validated -> Sent(sent_at_epoch_ms). Make ShardWorkflow fields private behind smart constructors.

findings.problem: status: String is a primitive that roams into the core. Status strings plus lifecycle booleans are the canonical anti-pattern that the skill mandates replacing with enums or typestate transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status to any arbitrary string ("", "SENT", "pending ", etc.) that the compiler cannot constrain. The lifecycle is not enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Define an enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and remove is_validated and is_sent entirely. The enum variants carry the lifecycle meaning.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a lifecycle boolean that, combined with is_sent: bool, permits 4 state combinations but only 3 are valid (Pending, Validated, Sent). This is wasted state space and a source of bugs.
findings.failure_mode: The invalid combination (is_validated=false, is_sent=true) represents a shard that was sent without validation. The type system cannot prevent this.
findings.fix: Eliminate the bool in favor of ShardState enum variants. If lifecycle data is needed per-state, embed it in the variant (e.g., Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }).

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a lifecycle boolean. sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is optional lifecycle data stored as a global field. This permits the invariant violation where is_sent=true but sent_at_epoch_ms=None, or is_sent=false but sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(123).
findings.failure_mode: Lifecycle data lives outside the variant that owns it. Consumers cannot trust that sent_at_epoch_ms is present when the shard is actually sent.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant: ShardState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. The u64 is non-optional because if the shard is sent, the timestamp must exist.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no preconditions. It does not verify that the shard is validated before marking it sent. It unconditionally overwrites status and sets is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can pass a fresh, unvalidated ShardWorkflow and mark it as sent. This is a silent business invariant violation with no error path.
findings.fix: Change the signature to accept a validated state explicitly: fn mark_sent(state: ShardState) -> ShardState. Use a typestate or enum where Validated is the only input to Sent, enforced by the compiler.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() to assign a hardcoded status string, allocating heap memory for a literal that could be an enum variant.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation in what appears to be a hot-path mutation. The string "sent" is allocated on every call.
findings.fix: Replace with an enum transition: state = ShardState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: timestamp }.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive. IDs that have domain rules (uniqueness, format, lifetime) should be newtyped.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can pass any string as an ID, including empty strings, duplicates, or values that do not represent valid shard identifiers. No domain constraint enforcement at the type level.
findings.fix: Define a ShardId newtype struct with a private field and a smart constructor: pub struct ShardId(String); impl ShardId { fn new(id: &str) -> Result<Self, InvalidIdError> { ... } }

findings.problem: All fields of ShardWorkflow are pub, exposing internal state to unrestricted mutation by any caller.
findings.failure_mode: Any crate consumer can set item.status = "anything" or item.is_validated = true directly, bypassing all invariants. The struct has no defensive encapsulation.
findings.fix: Make fields private. Provide smart constructors and state-transition methods. In the enum typestate design, the enum itself enforces valid transitions.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs a heap allocation (.to_string()) inside what should be a pure core function. The function name suggests a side-effecting action but it returns a mutated value, making the side effect implicit.
findings.failure_mode: Allocations hidden inside what appears to be a simple data transformation. Callers may not realize this function allocates per call.
findings.fix: Use an enum with a unit/variant pattern so no allocation is needed for state transitions. If the function needs I/O, keep it in the shell layer, not the core data transformation.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a raw u64 timestamp with no domain meaning. Timestamps carry rules (non-zero, monotonicity, timezone awareness) that should be encoded in the type.
findings.failure_mode: A caller could set sent_at_epoch_ms=0 or a nonsensical value. Option<u64> allows sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(0) to mean "no timestamp" which conflicts with is_sent=true.
findings.fix: Use a TimestampEpochMs newtype or embed the timestamp directly in the Sent variant as u64 (non-optional, since a sent shard must have a timestamp).

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation behavior
no profiler data for heap allocations in the hot path
no allocation audit for the .to_string() call on every mark_sent invocation
no command-truth evidence: no cargo check, cargo clippy, or cargo test commands were run
no behavior tests exist for the module at all
no formal specification of the ShardWorkflow lifecycle invariants
residual_risk: Static review only. The code compiles but represents illegal state combinations at the type level. mark_sent silently allows invalid transitions (unvalidated -> sent). No commands were run to verify compilation or test pass. The entire domain model needs replacement with an enum-based typestate to eliminate the fundamental invariant violations.
